angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 523,166 km at 19.68 pc = 0.36 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: distance 19.677 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 19.677 +/- 0.098 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 50.9432 +/- 0.0230 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00), 2215.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.752 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: radius 0.752 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.306 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 523,166 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4955 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: effective temperature 4955 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.031) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: effective temperature 4955 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.031) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 192263 (pscomppars): spectral type K2 V, from Paredes et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..176P/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 192263 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.03 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 192263 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.47, from Santos et al. 2003 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003A&A...406..373S/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 192263 (pscomppars): age 2.09 Gyr, from Dragomir et al. 2012 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012ApJ...754...37D/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 192263 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.8 km/s, from Santos et al. 2000 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2000A&A...356..599S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.61 from 2025A&A...698A..93J; the 28 published values span log g 4.14 to 4.76, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A%26A...698A..93J)
